activity.notes: Polyaenus describes Amage as the wife of the Sarmatian king Medosaccus who took over government, judged cases, stationed garrisons and repelled invasions. Modern scholarship dates the episode approximately 165-140 BCE and identifies her group more specifically with the Roxolani. Because the account is preserved in a later literary source, ATLAS marks the chronology as approximate and confidence as likely.

sources.title: Amazons ii. Amazons in the Iranian world — Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.citation_text: Encyclopaedia Iranica cites Polyaenus and places Amage as ruler of the Roxolani around 165-140 BCE.
